stem: According to the table, how many herons were counted at Cedar Pond in 2023?
stimulus:
Volunteers counted the herons at three wetlands in two consecutive years.

Herons Counted at Three Wetlands
Wetland | 2022 | 2023
North Marsh | 14 | 21
Cedar Pond | 9 | 17
Reed Flats | 26 | 12
explanation: Find the Cedar Pond row, then go across to the 2023 column. The cell where they meet says 17. This is the first move in every SAT question that asks what a table shows. If you can't land on the right cell every time, you won't be able to judge whether a claim matches the data.

A.why: You read the right row but the wrong column. 9 is Cedar Pond's count for 2022, not 2023.

C.why: You read the right column but the row above. 21 is North Marsh's 2023 count.

D.why: You read the right column but the row below. 12 is Reed Flats' 2023 count.

stem: According to the graph, in which month did the clinic record 60 visits?
stimulus: A community health clinic tracked how many people came in for a flu vaccination during each of four months.

figure.caption: Flu Vaccination Visits at a Community Clinic
figure.alt: Bar graph of flu vaccination visits by month, January through April.

explanation: Find 60 on the vertical axis and follow that gridline across until it meets the top of a bar. The March bar ends exactly there. Reading a bar against the axis this way is what lets you check a statement about a graph instead of trusting how it sounds.

A.why: The January bar stops at 30, two gridlines below 60. You may have counted gridlines without checking what each one is worth.

B.why: You chose the bar next to the right one. February stops at 45, one gridline short of 60.

D.why: You chose the bar on the other side of March. April stops at 15, well below 60.

stem: According to the table, what is the elevation of Marker C?
stimulus:
Surveyors placed four markers while mapping a coastal ridge. They recorded each marker's height and its distance inland.

Survey Markers on a Coastal Ridge
Marker | Elevation (meters) | Distance from coast (km)
A | 120 | 4
B | 85 | 9
C | 210 | 15
D | 160 | 22
explanation: Go to the Marker C row and read the cell under the Elevation (meters) column: 210. Checking the column header before you read the number is the habit that stops you from mixing up two measurements in a real data question.

A.why: You read the right row but the wrong column. 15 is Marker C's distance from the coast in kilometers, not its elevation.

B.why: You read the row above. 85 is Marker B's elevation.

D.why: You read the row below. 160 is Marker D's elevation.

stem: According to the graph, in which year was the average yield 10 kilograms per plant?
stimulus: Researchers at an agricultural station recorded the average tomato yield per plant in one test field each year from 2019 to 2023.

figure.caption: Average Tomato Yield in a Test Field, 2019–2023
figure.alt: Line graph of average tomato yield per plant for each year from 2019 to 2023.

explanation: Find 10 on the vertical axis, follow that gridline across to the point that sits on it, and drop straight down to the year axis. You land on 2021. Matching a point to its exact x and y values is the skill you need for any question that asks what a line graph shows in a particular year.

A.why: The 2019 point sits at 8, one gridline below 10. You probably misjudged which gridline the point touches.

B.why: You took the point just before the right one. 2020 is at 12, one gridline above 10.

D.why: You took the point just after the right one. 2022 is at 14, two gridlines above 10.
